new_statements.quote: L'accent tonique en béarnais affecte la dernière syllabe, lorsqu'elle est pleinement prononcée, et la pénultième, quand la dernière a un son faible. La règle de l'accent tonique béarnais s'explique facilement par l'origine latine de la presque totalité des mots qui composent notre idiome. Chez les Latins, l'accent tonique affectait une des trois dernières syllabes du mot. Ainsi dans les mots béarnais canta, chanter, termi, terme, limite, la syllabe accentuée est celle-là même qui l'était dans les mots latins cantare, terminus. Par la suppression des syllabes re, nus, l'accent béarnais porte sur la dernière syllabe dans canta, et sur la pénultième dans termi, au lieu de se trouver, comme en latin, sur la pénultième dans cantare, et sur l'antépénultième dans terminus.
new_statements.translation: The tonic accent in Béarnais falls on the last syllable when it is fully pronounced, and on the penult when the last one has a weak sound. The rule of the Béarnais tonic accent is easily explained by the Latin origin of almost all the words that make up our idiom. In Latin the tonic accent fell on one of the last three syllables of the word. Thus in the Béarnais words canta 'to sing', termi 'term, limit', the stressed syllable is the very one that was stressed in the Latin words cantare, terminus. Through the loss of the syllables re, nus, the Béarnais accent falls on the last syllable in canta and on the penult in termi, instead of falling, as in Latin, on the penult in cantare and on the antepenult in terminus.
new_statements.citation: Lespy, Vastin. 1880. Grammaire béarnaise, suivie d'un vocabulaire béarnais-français. 2e édition. Paris: Maisonneuve. 'Additions et corrections', p. 503, re-quoting the 1st edition (1858), Introduction, p. xvi.
new_statements.locator: 1880 ed. p. 503 (p. 517 of 538), 'Additions et corrections'; = 1858 ed. Introduction pp. xvi-xvii
new_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (538 pp.). extracted text of p. 517 and a rendered image of that page show the heading 'ADDITIONS ET CORRECTIONS' with printed page numbers 502 (PDF 516) and 504 (PDF 518) on either side, so printed p. 503 is right. The quoted passage is there in full, in quotation marks, closed by '— Gram. béarnaise, 1re édit., p. XVI'. Minor differences: the printed 1880 text reads 'l'accent tanique affectait' (a printer's typo, visible in the page scan; the scanned also has 'tanique'), which the compiler silently normalised to 'tonique'; the scanned's 'canta^' is just 'canta,' in print. Everything else matches word for word. The same passage is in the 1858 first edition file ( lines 801-845, print…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is on one of the last two syllables and is determined by the shape of the final syllable: final stress when the last syllable has a full vowel (e.g. infinitives in -a < -are, words in consonant), penult stress when the final syllable has a weak/reduced vowel (final -e, -o/-a of feminines etc.); the position is the inherited Latin stressed syllable. The modern Aranese academy grammar (IEA 2020: 24-25) is consistent (default final stress in consonant-final words, penult in vowel/-s-final words, exceptions carry a written accent) and adds that a few proparoxytones (musica, gramatica, politica) survive but tend to become paroxytone. Because the position is lexically fixed per word rather than computed from syllable weight in the strict sense, a 'lexical (unpredictable) (final/penult window)' reading is also defensible.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned by Lespy. Millardet 1910 (Landais Gascon atlas, p. 212) marks an 'accent secondaire' inside phonic groups but gives no rule.
new_statements.exceptions: Lespy: none stated beyond the two-way rule. IEA 2020 (Aranese): residual proparoxytones (musica, gramatica, politica) tending to become paroxytone; words whose stress departs from the default carry a written accent (oxytones in vowel/vowel+s such as veirà, francés, decidís, Salardú; paroxytones in consonant or diphthong such as córrer, parlàuem, notícia; 3pl future parlaràn; some verb forms in -en, -ii; a few monosyllables tà, é, qué).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, citation forms, described for Béarnais (bear1240), a Gascon dialect; Lespy characterises the accent as an 'élévation de ton' on one of the last syllables and explains it etymologically. The corroborating IEA grammars describe Aranese (aran1260), another Gascon dialect; no Gascon-wide modern statement was opened.
new_statements.identity_note: gasc1241 is a retired bookkeeping code (ISO gsc merged into oci in 2007); the live Glottolog languoid is Gascon gasc1240 (dialect of Occitan) with sub-dialects Aranese aran1260, Béarnais bear1240, Landais land1254 etc. The quoted statement describes Béarnais (bear1240); the corroborating Institut d'Estudis Aranesi grammars describe Aranese (aran1260); Millardet describes Landais (land1254). No opened source describes Gascon as a whole.

sources.note: Béarnais word stress falls on the final syllable when it is 'fully pronounced' and on the penult when the final has a 'weak sound'; explained as inheritance of the Latin stressed syllable (canta < cantare, termi < terminus). Nothing on secondary stress.

sources.citation: Lespy, Vastin. 1858. Grammaire béarnaise, suivie d'un vocabulaire français-béarnais. Paris: Maisonneuve (1st ed.), Introduction pp. XVI-XVII.
sources.note: Same rule as the 1880 re-quotation (scanned slightly garbled here): 'Dans le béarnais, l'accent tonique affecte la dernière syllabe, lorsqu'elle est pleinement prononcée, et la pénultième, quand la dernière a un son faible'; defines the tonic accent as an 'élévation de ton' on one of the last syllables; says the idiom is 'très accentué'.

Gascon/Aranese pages say nothing about stress placement (Aranese: acute accent 'marks lexical stress' on i/u). 'Occitan phonology' gives the general Occitan rule (oxytone if final syllable ends in consonant or in a diphthong in -u/-i, paroxytone if it ends in a vowel or vowel+s; antepenult only in Niçard/Cisalpine) with no Gascon-specific note and no citation.

sources.citation: Institut d'Estudis Aranesi - Acadèmia aranesa dera lengua occitana. 2020. Gramatica der occitan aranés (1èra edicion, juriòl 2020; ISBN 978-84-09-22141-7). Section 2.3 'Accentuacion', pp. 24-25.
sources.note: Aranese (Gascon of the Val d'Aran) retains some proparoxytones (/'myzika/, /gra'matika/, /pu'litika/) which tend to become paroxytone (/my'ziko/ etc.); the written-accent rules then encode stress: oxytones ending in vowel or vowel+s and paroxytones ending in consonant other than s or in diphthong are the marked cases (so the default is final stress in consonant-final words and penult stress in vowel/-s-final words). No explicit prose rule of default stress placement; nothing on secondary stress.
